There are six domestic commercial plants and one international producer supplying the U.S. market. Three of the plants are conversions of petroleum refineries—World Energy, Montana Renewables, and Phillips 66. Diamond Green Diesel was a conversion and expansion of an existing diesel plant while LanzaJet and New Rise Renewables are new plants. Neste, an international producer, has plants in Finland, the Netherlands, and Singapore. Neste began exporting to the United States in 2020 with deliveries to a Northern California terminal, and annual production capacity was 515 million gallons (or 34,000 barrels/day) as of May 2025 (Neste 2020, 2025). Total domestic SAF consumption in 2025 was 281 million gallons (Figure 2, EPA 2025). The new plants contributed to a significant increase in in consumption from domestically produced SAF increasing from 39 million gallons in 2024 to 241 million gallons in 2025 (EPA 2025). The International Air Transit Association (IATA) estimates 2025 global production of 627 million gallons with domestic production representing about 38% of the total (IATA 2025a, EPA 2025). Imports from Neste supplied 65% of U.S. SAF in 2024 but dropped to 14% in the 2025 (Figure 3, EPA 2025).
